units.translation: Bamberger corrected it thus; what is in M is καὶ τὰ χρέα ἔπη, changed by Turnebus to τὰ χρεῖ᾽ ἔπη. In a different sense Theocritus 25, 6 said ὁδοῦ ζαχρεῖον ὁδίτην, meaning 'in need of the road': which is the usual meaning of the adjective χρεῖος, as Aeschylus himself a little later at v. 202 said χρεῖος εἶ ξένη φυγάς. Different is the Homeric ζαχρηής, written by some as ζαχρειής and explained variously by others, on which see Thes. vol. 4 p. 10.
Answer the strangers with words of reverence, lamentation, and great need.

Thus M, not ζεύγλησι, which is in some copies, where Hermann says: "ζεύγλην some say is the curvature of the yoke, others the part into which the neck of the animal is inserted, or, what is the same, the straps, which are called subiugia by the Latins. In this sense Aeschylus used it here, and before him Homer Il. 19, 405 πᾶσα δὲ χαίτη ζεύγλης ἐξεριποῦσα παρὰ ζυγὸν | οὐδας ἵκανεν. See the Homeric scholiasts and Scheffer on vehicles p. 116 ff."
